why_trail.why: Floor proven by command, not asserted - and the proof immediately earned its keep. The first advance REFUSED on c2: tests/test_retirement_guard.py::test_canon_is_clean went red with 6 unapproved-store-mention violations, all in my own notes-1.md, which sat at the repo root and therefore counted as a new SHIPPED site naming the episode store. The guard is correct and I was the regression: its whole purpose is that constraint:episodes-are-not-prescriptions is easy to break by accident, and a root-level file discussing apply_episode_delta.py is exactly the shape it watches for. Fixed by moving the run artifact into the run's own area (.agent-work/epic-418-followon/commander-f2/notes-1.md) rather than by adding six transient lines to a frozen approval census - a working note is not doctrine and should not enter a census that exists to make new mentions expensive. Suite now 0 failed. This is the cold critic's finding 7 vindicated inside twenty minutes: the previous plan attested a hardcoded baseline that nothing verified, and would have carried this regression silently into five downstream gates that all leaned on that same baseline.

The identity question is settled as a FLEET-WIDE position, not an MCP-local trade, and that reframe is the gate's real output. The Admiral found the same defect mid-gate in a second, independent seam (#549, spine_rail.py): its binding file IS keyed per agent, but session_view() merges the bare sid key and every sid#agent key into one flat map and decide_stop takes the first non-foreign entry - the discriminator exists and a merge two functions later discards it, while the _foreign_worktree guard cannot help because every child entry inherited the parent's worktree from CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR. Same shape as the door, twice, neither aware of the other: the harness shares the container and we put identity in the container. So the recorded rule is about GRANULARITY, not about arguments - identity may be bound to a container only at the granularity that container genuinely separates, and a seam below that granularity fails closed. That form is forced by the hook seam, which has no per-call argument for identity to ride on; 'move identity to the call' would have fixed one seam and left the other with no expressible remedy. Option A is rejected on evidence rather than taste: it covers a subagent naming its own spine but not one naming its parent's, which is the actual failure, and the CLI is ALREADY the per-call-identity door, so A adds no capability the repo lacks while deleting the only property distinguishing the two doors. The pin is deliberately outcome-neutral - it encodes 'the binding is what the record says', not 'option C is right' - and I confirmed it is not vacuous before handing it over: two distinct mutations of the REAL door (a per-call spine_file argument on spine_status; a late-bound SPINE re-read per access) turned it red on two DIFFERENT tests, and the door restored to an empty git diff. The authoritative mutation is still the reviewer's.

Four independent review passes, four genuine defeats of the pin, all four findings taken. Closing on the Admiral's stopping rule: no fifth pass, because the marginal value of one is below the cost of not reaching g4b, the epic's entry condition for C. The fourth finding was fixed rather than shipped around - assertIn became assertEqual - and applying it exposed the deeper limit that black-box argument fuzzing cannot establish a property over all argument names, which is why the final pin is structural and mentions no argument names at all. Six mutation classes red across the pair.

g1 closes with the identity position recorded as a fleet-wide rule about container granularity, a property given up that is named rather than gestured at, and a pin that four independent reviewers each defeated and that now holds against all six of their and my mutation classes. The four one-line findings are the gate's most reusable output: a pin over declarations is a pin over intentions; an enumeration is not a property; a property over the calls you make says nothing about the answers you invent; containment is not equality.
